external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A person who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: The Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders. It is exposed to the internet.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run. It is the only thing we expose to the internet.
processes.notes: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders and reads and writes the orders database.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network; it is not exposed outside.
processes.notes: The database password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)
data_stores.notes: The order service accesses it with a single application account that has full read/write.

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_stores.notes: The receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.

data_flows.name: browse storefront
data_flows.description: Shopper browsing activity sent to the storefront API.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Shopper credentials submitted to the storefront API for sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: Shopper order submissions sent to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service to submit an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders and related shopper data in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The application account password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for each completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone containing the storefront API and shoppers accessing it.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The internal network containing the order service and orders database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

trust_boundaries.name: Cloud Storage
trust_boundaries.description: The Cloud Storage hosting zone containing the receipt archive.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

assumptions.assumption: The shopper is outside the system's control and is represented in a separate tenant trust zone.
assumptions.basis: The text describes shoppers as external people interacting with the storefront.

assumptions.assumption: The shopper's email and password are credentials held by or associated with the shopper.
assumptions.basis: The text states that shoppers sign in with email and password.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API is availability-critical to the checkout and order-capture path.
assumptions.basis: The text describes the storefront API as the path through which shoppers browse and place orders.

assumptions.assumption: The order service handles business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the order service processes orders and reads and writes shopper and payment-related data.
The database contains shopper addresses and card-last-four data, which are personal and payment-related data.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The archive contains receipts associated with completed orders.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is in a separate tenant-controlled Cloud Storage zone.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the receipt archive as a Cloud Storage bucket, which is a separately hosted storage service.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive holds financial and business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It stores receipts for completed orders in the checkout and order-capture path.

assumptions.assumption: The settlement webhook carries financial information.
assumptions.basis: The card processor settles payments and reports that an order is paid.
